evals.prompt: Build a landing page for Ledgerly, a bookkeeping app for freelance designers. Single self-contained HTML file. No brand guidelines yet, use whatever looks good.
evals.expected_output: An aesthetic direction proposed under the Default Style Guide and awaiting approval, then (after approval) a single index.html using only the four default colors, followed by an Implementation step report and a Final Report.
expectations: Proposed an aesthetic direction and waited for approval before writing any code
The Design Thinking step report names the Default Style Guide as the style source, because the user gave no explicit brief
After approval, wrote one HTML file whose colors are limited to #000000, #FFFFFF, #6B7280 and #22C55E, plus status colors on text only
Bright Green #22C55E is never used as a background color

Uses no row of the ban table under Avoid in references/aesthetics-guide.md: no Inter, Roboto, Arial or system font stack, no gradient of any color, no glow, no eyebrow labels and no pill-shaped buttons
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE or PARTIAL and the file name
The Final Report has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines; Evidence names the contrast check result, and Uncertainty records the visual check as untested when no browser was used

evals.prompt: Our brand colors are navy #0B1F3A and coral #FF6F59, with Fraunces for headings. Design a pricing section with three plans as a React component for our Next.js marketing site. Just build it, no need to check the direction with me first.
evals.expected_output: The direction stated in one line without waiting, then a React pricing component using the brand palette and Fraunces, followed by an Implementation step report and a Final Report.
expectations: Stated the aesthetic direction in one line and did not wait for approval, because the user said to just build it
Uses the navy and coral brand colors instead of the Default Style Guide palette
Uses Fraunces for headings
Delivers a React component (JSX or TSX), not plain HTML
Each plan has a CTA button with hover, focus and active states
Every text and background pair meets 4.5:1 contrast, or the Final Report lists the failing pair with its ratio
The Final Report opens with Result: and its status, and its Decision: line names the pending choice or says No approval needed

evals.prompt: Create an admin dashboard page for a small warehouse team: stock levels table, low-stock alerts, and a shipments-today counter. Plain HTML/CSS/JS is fine.
evals.expected_output: An aesthetic direction awaiting approval, then a dashboard with a table, alerts and counter using the default palette, status colors on text only, followed by step reports and a Final Report.
expectations: Proposed an aesthetic direction and waited for approval before writing any code
Low-stock alerts use the Warning or Danger color only on text, never as a background
The stock table has an empty state with a recovery message
Shadows appear only on floating elements (menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts), never on static cards or sections, and no card sits inside another card
The Implementation step report lists the visual, contrast, quality and build checks with their results
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying the status and the files written, and has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines

evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the page's purpose and target audience (and any brand or style constraints) and writes no code.
expectations: Asked for the purpose and the target audience before proposing a direction
Wrote no code and no file
If the run ends without an answer, the Final Report status is BLOCKED and the Decision: line names the missing information

evals.prompt: Build a super minimalist portfolio homepage for a photographer, but with lots of flashy animations everywhere.
evals.expected_output: The skill names the conflict between minimalism and heavy animation and asks which takes priority before writing code.
expectations: Named the conflict between the minimalist direction and the request for many animations
Asked which constraint takes priority instead of picking one silently
Wrote no code before the user answered

evals.prompt: Add a React settings page to the app in ../../eval-fixtures/frontend-design/vue-repo with a profile form and a notifications toggle.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the repo first, sees it is a Vue project, and confirms the framework before generating code instead of writing React JSX into it.
expectations: Read package.json or App.vue and noticed the project uses Vue, not React
Asked the user to confirm the framework before generating code
Wrote no React JSX into the Vue project
The proposal lists the files it would create or modify

expectations: frontend-design did not trigger
No frontend code was written

evals.prompt: Build a signup page for Fieldnote, a note-taking app for field botanists, as a single self-contained HTML file with a short form and a plan picker. No brand or style preferences. Just build it.
evals.expected_output: The direction stated in one line, then one HTML file that follows the no-brief defaults: tokens for the four colors, no ban-table element, interface motion under 300 ms with faster exits and a reduced-motion fallback, sentence case and two weights, followed by an Implementation step report and a Final Report.
expectations: Stated the aesthetic direction in one line and did not wait for approval, because the user said to just build it
The page has no gradient of any color, no glow, no grain or noise texture, no staggered section reveal, no scroll-triggered entrance and no bounce or overshoot easing
Every transition or animation lasts under 300 ms, each exit is shorter than its entry, and a prefers-reduced-motion media query removes or reduces the movement

Colors are declared once as CSS custom properties limited to #000000, #FFFFFF, #6B7280 and #22C55E (plus status colors on text only), and component rules use only those properties, with no raw hex value outside the declaration
Page and container backgrounds are white or black, and #22C55E appears only on an active, selected or checked state (the chosen plan, a checked box, a focused field), never as a fill or decoration
Headings, buttons and labels use sentence case, and the CSS uses at most two font weights
Shadows appear only on floating elements, and no card sits inside another card
The Implementation step report has a Visual check line (screenshots at phone and desktop width against the ban table, or untested with a reason) and a Subtraction pass line

evals.prompt: Add a pricing section with three plans to the page in ../../eval-fixtures/frontend-design/rules-repo. Just build it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads DESIGN.md before proposing, names it as the style source, adds the pricing section following every rule in it, leaves DESIGN.md unchanged, and offers any new rule line only as an optional proposal.
expectations: Read DESIGN.md before proposing a direction, and the Design Thinking step report names it on the Style source line
The pricing section uses only the custom properties in :root, adding any new color there first, with no hex value inside a component rule
Headings use Fraunces at 600 and body text Source Serif 4 at 400, with no other weight
Buttons, plan containers and any inputs have a 2px radius
The section is separated by a 1px --color-border top rule and 96px of vertical padding, with no section background color
DESIGN.md is not modified; any new rule line appears only as an optional proposal after the Final Report Decision: text, quoted with the file name

evals.prompt: Design a clean, modern, premium settings page for a password manager. Single HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A proposed direction, awaiting approval, that replaces "clean", "modern" and "premium" with concrete decisions or a named reference, before any code is written.
expectations: Proposed an aesthetic direction and waited for approval before writing any code

The proposed direction turns "clean", "modern" and "premium" into concrete decisions (for example the typefaces, the two weights, the spacing scale, the radius, borders instead of shadows) or a named reference with the properties taken from it
The direction does not describe the style with only vague words such as clean, modern, premium, elegant or professional
The Design Thinking step report records the vague-word conversion

evals.prompt: Build a launch hero for Aurora, a weather app, as a single HTML file. I want a big purple-to-orange gradient background behind the hero and a maximalist feel with a grain texture. Just build it.
evals.expected_output: The hero is built with the requested purple-to-orange gradient and grain in a maximalist direction; the Quality Bar passes both as brief-requested, while contrast and reduced motion still apply.
expectations: The hero background is a purple-to-orange gradient, because the brief asked for it
A grain texture is present and the direction is maximalist, not toned down to the Default Style Guide
The Quality Bar and the Final Report treat the gradient and grain as requested by the brief, not as ban-table failures
Text on the gradient meets WCAG AA contrast, or the Final Report lists the failing pair with its ratio
Any animation is disabled or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion
